more: Both river crabs spawn at 2:55, and the fight for one is usually decided by which mid laner gets there first.
If your wave is stuck under your tower, leaving costs minions and you still arrive second, so trading crabs is the better deal.
An even swap of crabs is a fine result. Losing a crab and your jungler's life is not.
check: Whether your wave is actually pushed, and which river your jungler is walking toward.

more: A jungler who hasn't shown where his route should put him is a warning, not good news.
Backing off costs you a couple of minions. Dying costs the wave, the next wave and your tower plates.
Once he appears somewhere else, you get a short window to push hard again.
check: When and where their jungler was last seen, and whether you have a ward in river on either side.

more: A kill only counts if he also loses the minions. If the wave sits in the middle, he walks back to it and has lost little.
The tower kills a crashed wave for you, which also resets the lane so it pushes back toward you later.
With him dead, the river is yours for his death timer. That's the time for a deep ward or an objective.
check: How big the wave is and how low you are, and whether an objective is up right now.

A melee champion has to cross the whole lane to farm it, with your jungler behind him. Most just lose the minions.
A few waves of this turns a small lead into a full item gap before the mid game starts.
check: Whether the enemy wave is slightly bigger than yours, and where the wave is sitting.

more: Near your tower he can't trade freely and a gank on you is much harder, so the lead stops growing.

The player who is behind catches up by collecting every wave, not by winning a fight.

If an objective is up, a shoved mid wave is what lets your team start it without being interrupted.
check: His respawn timer, and whether a dragon or the grubs are available.

If you reach level six and your first item without dying, the lane has gone to plan even if you're down minions.
check: Where the wave is sitting, and whether their jungler has been seen recently.

Every wave that dies to his tower is gold and experience he doesn't get, so a failed roam leaves him behind.
If the roam does work, your plates and levels are the payment your team gets back.
check: Which way he walked, and whether your side lane is pushed up or safe at its tower.

check: How much of your wave is left, and whether your jungler is close enough for a play elsewhere.

A fast push gets you out now but gives a short window, since the wave is small.
Stack the wave before a recall or a deep ward. Fast push when an objective or fight is already starting.
check: How long until you need to move, and whether he can clear a big wave quickly.

Showing briefly to clear and then disappearing keeps you safe and keeps them guessing.

A mid wave pushing by itself forces someone to come and clear it, which is one fewer enemy at the objective.
Don't keep standing mid for the next tower alone. The gain is the map behind it.
check: Which objective spawns next and when, and where your jungler is.

more: Teleport is worth spending when it saves a whole stacked wave and tower plates. A few minions aren't worth it.
If you walk, buy first. Coming back with an item matters more than arriving a few seconds sooner.
After a death the wave usually pushes toward you, which is a safe place to farm and rebuild.
check: Whether Teleport is off cooldown, and how big the wave heading to your tower is.
breaks: If an objective fight is close, keep Teleport for that and walk to lane.

Small wins like this add up to a recall he has to take at a bad time.
